short: The 1215 charter that first bound an English king to written law.
full:
Magna Carta was sealed at Runnymede on 15 June 1215 by King John, under duress from rebellious barons who had already taken London. Most of its sixty-three clauses address the specific grievances of a feudal elite — scutage, wardship, fish weirs — rather than any general principle of liberty.

Its significance is what later generations made of it. Clause 39, guaranteeing that no free man be imprisoned or dispossessed except by lawful judgment of his peers or by the law of the land, became the seed of due process and habeas corpus. Annulled by the Pope within ten weeks, it was reissued repeatedly and passed into English law, and from there into the American Constitution and the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
